headline: Sensex Flat, Nifty Gains 53 Points as Metals and Smallcaps Surge
why: Metals and FMCG stocks saw strong gains amid easing global oil prices.
Moody's raised India's FY27 growth forecast to 7% despite inflation risks.
US stock gains and falling crude oil retreat eased immediate global inflation fears.
Smallcap and midcap stocks outperformed broader indices with strong buying interest.
whatHappening: India's foreign exchange reserves fell by $4.9 billion to $780.8 billion.
Securities Transaction Tax (STT) collections surged 53% to ₹40,214 crore in FY27.
Hi-Tech Flow Solutions filed DRHP to raise ₹300 crore via an IPO.
Indian sovereign bonds suffered a fifth weekly loss following Fed rate hike expectations.

stocksInNews.sources: Metals sector rally led market gains with 1.5% jump
IT sector under pressure ahead of US Fed decision
Weakness in IT stocks dragged broader benchmark indices
FMCG sector shined as defensive buying picked up
Easing crude oil prices supported energy sector sentiment
Banking sector traded rangebound amid surging bond yields
Financials held steady following upgraded GDP growth forecast
Steady institutional interest during broad market recovery
Moody's 7% GDP growth forecast boosted industrial capex outlook
Auto sector stayed mixed amid ongoing inflation warnings

summary:
Indian equity markets ended mixed as Nifty gained supported by metals and smallcaps, while IT heavyweights dragged the Sensex.
Moody's upgraded India's FY27 GDP growth forecast to 7%, providing underlying optimism despite dropping forex reserves and rising bond yields.
Meanwhile, STT tax collections surged 53%, underscoring robust retail participation and equity trading volumes.
